class.name: MediaSource
class.brief_description: Reads a media file (Matroska/WebM, MP4/MOV, MPEG-TS, AVI, and music files) or a network stream with FFmpeg: video access units for a hardware decoder, decoded audio for an [AudioStreamMedia].
class.description: Opens a file with FFmpeg's libavformat and reads it on a worker thread. The video stream is only demuxed: its access units go, in Annex-B for H.264 and HEVC (converted from MP4/Matroska's length-prefixed form with the [code]h264_mp4toannexb[/code] / [code]hevc_mp4toannexb[/code] bitstream filters), through a bounded queue to a [V4L2Decoder] ([method V4L2Decoder.open_source], [method HWVideoTexture.open_source]). The first access unit after [method open] and after every [method seek] is a keyframe with the parameter sets (VPS/SPS/PPS) in band. Files on a file share open by URL: [code]smb://host/share/path/file.mkv[/code] (SMB2/3, see [method set_smb_credentials] and [member network_buffer_size]). A thread of their own reads them ahead into a ring buffer, so network latency doesn't reach the demuxer. Files and streams also open by [code]http://[/code], [code]https://[/code] and [code]udp://[/code] URL, through a readahead ring of their own (see [method open], [member network_tls_verify] and [member live_latency]). A live stream (MPEG-TS over UDP, or HTTP without a length) can't seek: [method is_live], [method is_seekable]. Music files (MP3, FLAC, Ogg Vorbis/Opus, WAV, AAC/M4A, ALAC, AC-3, DTS, TrueHD) play like a film without video: [method get_video_info] is empty, and the audio is the clock. A cover picture in the file is not taken for the video: it is in [method get_album_art] and [method get_attached_pictures], and the file's tags are in [method get_tags]. Subtitle tracks can be selected too ([method select_subtitle_track], [method read_subtitle_event]): text tracks are decoded to text, ASS lines and styled runs, bitmap tracks to RGBA images with their rectangles. The selected audio track is decoded and resampled with libswresample to stereo float at the [AudioServer] mix rate, into a ring buffer that [method get_audio_stream] plays. More than two channels are downmixed (centre and surrounds at -3 dB, LFE dropped); the source layout is in [method get_audio_tracks]. The playback position of that stream is the A/V master clock. All times are media seconds: the stream timestamp minus the file's start time ([method get_start_time]), so the first frame is at about 0. The thread blocks when the queues are full ([member video_queue_seconds], [member audio_queue_seconds]) and is woken when they are consumed; it never spins. [codeblock] var source := MediaSource.new() if source.open("/path/film.mkv") == OK: print(source.get_info()) video.open_source(source) # HWVideoTexture $AudioStreamPlayer.stream = source.get_audio_stream() [/codeblock]

method.name: add_external_subtitle
method.description: Loads a subtitle file (SubRip, ASS/SSA or WebVTT; a local path or smb://) as one more subtitle track after the file's own, and returns its index, or -1 if it can't be read ([method get_last_error] says why; the source keeps playing). Blocking: it reads the whole file (up to 16 MiB). Text in UTF-8, UTF-16 with a byte order mark, or anything else read as Windows-1252. [param language] and [param title] default to what the file name says ([method MediaBrowser.parse_subtitle_name]) and the file name. The track is selected like any other; its events are all handed out by [method read_subtitle_event] at once, in time order, and again from the events still showing at the target after a [method seek]. [method close] drops the files. Find the files with [method MediaBrowser.find_subtitles].

method.name: close
method.description: Stops the thread and closes the file. Close a [V4L2Decoder] reading from it first.

method.name: get_album_art
method.description: Returns the cover of a music file as an [Image]: the picture marked as the front cover (by its title, as ID3 and FLAC name them) if there is one, else the first attached picture that decodes (PNG, JPEG, WebP, BMP). [code]null[/code] if there is none. It decodes the picture on each call: keep the result.

method.name: get_audio_position
method.description: Returns the media time of the next audio frame to be mixed: the time of the last frame mixed plus one frame. Right after [method seek] it is the seek target.

method.name: get_audio_channel_stream
method.description: Returns a new [AudioStreamMedia] that plays one channel of the audio as mono, for an [AudioStreamPlayer3D] placed where that speaker would be. Needs [member discrete_channels]. [param channel]: 0 FL, 1 FR, 2 FC, 3 LFE, 4 BL, 5 BR, 6 SL, 7 SR (FFmpeg's 7.1 order); [method get_audio_channels] says which the track has. A 5.1 track has either the back pair (FFmpeg's "5.1") or the side pair ("5.1(side)", as on most Blu-rays); other layouts' channels are mixed into the nearest of the eight. Night mode's gain and the dialogue boost (on FC) apply to the channels as to the stereo mix. Silent while [member playback_speed] isn't 1.

method.name: get_audio_channels
method.description: Returns the eight channel slots of [method get_audio_channel_stream], one Dictionary each: [code]index[/code], [code]name[/code] ("FL", "FR", "FC", "LFE", "BL", "BR", "SL", "SR"), [code]label[/code] ("front left", ...) and [code]present[/code] (the playing track has it; all false until its first audio is decoded).

method.name: get_audio_stream
method.description: Returns a new [AudioStreamMedia] that plays the decoded audio. Play it from one [AudioStreamPlayer] at a time.

method.name: get_attached_pictures
method.description: Returns the pictures stored in the file (cover art in MP3, FLAC, M4A and Ogg, and Matroska covers stored as a picture stream): one Dictionary each, [code]codec[/code] ("png", "mjpeg", ...), [code]title[/code] (for example "Cover (front)"; may be empty), [code]data[/code] (the encoded picture), [code]image[/code] (an [Image], or [code]null[/code] if the format can't be decoded) and [code]size[/code] (a [Vector2i]). These streams are never chosen as the video. Each call decodes them again.

method.name: get_audio_track
method.description: Returns the selected audio track (index into [method get_audio_tracks]), or -1.

method.name: get_bit_rate
method.description: Returns the container's overall bit rate in bit/s (all streams), or 0 if it doesn't say.

method.name: get_chapter_at
method.description: Returns the index of the chapter playing at [param seconds], or -1 before the first chapter, after the last one ends, or when the file has none.

method.name: get_chapters
method.description: Returns the file's chapters (Matroska, MP4): one Dictionary each, [code]index[/code], [code]start[/code], [code]end[/code] (media seconds, like every time here) and [code]title[/code] (may be empty), sorted by start. A chapter without an end lasts until the next one. Empty if the file has none.

method.name: get_audio_tracks
method.description: Returns one Dictionary per audio stream: [code]index[/code], [code]stream_index[/code], [code]codec[/code], [code]channels[/code], [code]channel_layout[/code] (for example "5.1(side)"), [code]sample_rate[/code], [code]bit_rate[/code], [code]language[/code] (as the file says it), [code]language_code[/code] ([method normalize_language]), [code]title[/code], [code]default[/code], [code]commentary[/code] and [code]visual_impaired[/code] (audio description; both from the stream's flags or its title).

method.name: get_duration
method.description: Returns the duration in seconds (0 if unknown).

method.name: get_info
method.description: Returns [code]path[/code], [code]format[/code], [code]duration[/code], [code]start_time[/code], [code]bit_rate[/code], [code]video[/code] ([method get_video_info]), [code]audio_tracks[/code], [code]subtitle_tracks[/code], [code]chapters[/code] ([method get_chapters]), [code]audio_track[/code], [code]subtitle_track[/code], [code]output_rate[/code], [code]tags[/code] ([method get_tags]), [code]attached_pictures[/code] (how many; see [method get_attached_pictures]), [code]live[/code] ([method is_live]), [code]seekable[/code] ([method is_seekable]) and [code]network_description[/code] (for http, https and udp, for example "HTTPS from host (7.7 MB, seekable)" or "UDP port 1234 (live, 416 KiB socket buffer)", the buffer the kernel granted, capped by [code]net.core.rmem_max[/code]; else empty).

method.name: get_external_subtitle_count
method.description: Returns how many subtitle files [method add_external_subtitle] has added since [method open].

method.name: get_last_error
method.description: Returns the last error or warning (a failed seek or an audio track that can't be decoded don't stop the source).

method.name: get_letterbox
method.description: Where the picture is inside the frame, from [member letterbox_detection]: [code]enabled[/code], [code]known[/code] (3 frames with a picture were scanned; until then [code]rect[/code] is the whole frame), [code]done[/code] (final: 6 such frames, or 40 keyframes scanned), [code]rect[/code] (a [Rect2i] in [code]frame_size[/code] pixels, the decoded picture's size, which is the visible size of [method get_video_info]), [code]uv_rect[/code] (the same as fractions of the frame, a [Rect2]), [code]bars[/code] (the rect is smaller than the frame), [code]picture_aspect[/code] (the rect's display aspect, pixel aspect included; for side-by-side 3D, both eyes together), [code]frames[/code], [code]frame_times[/code] (media seconds of the frames used), [code]scanned[/code], [code]dark[/code] (keyframes that were black or too dark to count), [code]cpu_seconds[/code] (CPU time of the detector's thread so far), [code]decode_seconds_max[/code] (the slowest keyframe) and [code]error[/code] (for example: no software decoder for the codec). Poll it now and then; it doesn't change once [code]done[/code].

method.name: get_output_rate
method.description: Returns the sample rate of the decoded audio: the [AudioServer] mix rate when the file was opened.

method.name: get_path
method.description: Returns the path given to [method open].

method.name: get_position
method.description: Returns [method get_audio_position] if an audio track is selected, else the PTS of the last video access unit taken from the queue.

method.name: get_secondary_subtitle_track
method.description: Returns the second subtitle track of dual subtitles ([method select_secondary_subtitle_track]), or -1.

method.name: get_seek_target
method.description: Returns the target of the last [method seek] (0 after [method open]).

method.name: get_serial
method.description: Returns the seek count. Video access units carry the serial they were read under.

method.name: get_start_time
method.description: Returns the file's start time in seconds, which is subtracted from every timestamp.

method.name: get_state
method.description: Returns the state.

method.name: get_stats
method.description: Returns counters: [code]bitrate_bps[/code] (the video bit rate at the playback position, over the last 3 whole seconds with data; left out while unknown, see [method get_video_bitrate_history]), [code]packets_read[/code], [code]bytes_read[/code], [code]video_packets[/code], [code]video_bytes[/code], [code]video_skipped[/code] (before the first keyframe, and in trick play all but the keyframes shown), [code]video_parameter_sets_added[/code], [code]video_queue[/code], [code]video_queue_bytes[/code], [code]audio_packets[/code], [code]audio_frames_out[/code], [code]audio_decode_errors[/code], [code]audio_dropped_frames[/code] (before a seek target), [code]audio_silence_frames[/code], [code]audio_buffered[/code] (seconds), [code]audio_position[/code], [code]audio_underruns[/code] (the ring ran empty during playback), [code]audio_seek_waits[/code] (it was empty before the first frame after open or a seek: expected, the position holds), [code]audio_frames_mixed[/code], [code]audio_finished[/code], [code]read_errors[/code], [code]seeks[/code], [code]seek_retries[/code], [code]trick_steps[/code] and [code]trick_play_speed[/code] ([method trick_play]), [code]external_clock[/code], [code]external_clock_error_ms[/code] (the audio position minus the external clock at the last read) and [code]external_clock_ratio[/code] (the resampling rate: above 1 to catch up) for [method set_external_clock], [code]subtitle_events[/code], [code]subtitle_decode_errors[/code], [code]subtitle_queue[/code], [code]thread_cpu_seconds[/code] (CPU time of the demux thread), [code]serial[/code], [code]eof[/code], [code]state[/code], [code]state_name[/code], [code]last_error[/code], [code]network[/code] ([code]true[/code] for smb://, http://, https:// and udp://), [code]live[/code] ([method is_live]), [code]night_mode[/code], [code]night_mode_decoder_drc[/code] (the track is AC-3 or E-AC-3: night mode also uses the stream's own DRC), [code]dialogue_boost_applies[/code] (the audio has a centre channel), [code]audio_gain_db[/code] (night mode's gain just now), [code]audio_limiter_db[/code] (the limiter's reduction, 0 or negative), [code]audio_typical_level_db[/code]. For smb:// files also: [code]net_buffer_bytes[/code] (ring size), [code]net_buffered_bytes[/code] (read ahead of the demuxer's position), [code]net_bytes_read[/code], [code]net_requests[/code], [code]net_resets[/code] (seeks outside the buffered range), [code]net_waits[/code] (reads that had to wait for the network), [code]net_seek_waits[/code] (of those, waits while the buffer refilled after open or a seek: expected), [code]net_stalls[/code] and [code]net_stall_seconds[/code] (waits once the buffer had refilled: the network didn't keep up), [code]net_wait_seconds[/code], [code]net_refills[/code] (refills done: from open or a seek until 4 MiB were read ahead), [code]net_refill_seconds[/code], [code]net_refill_mbps[/code] (the read rate during refills, which bounds how fast a seek settles: the decoder needs everything from the keyframe before the target), [code]net_reconnects[/code], [code]net_errors[/code], [code]net_read_mbps[/code] (Mbit/s while requests were in flight: the link's rate), [code]net_average_mbps[/code] (since open), [code]net_busy_seconds[/code], [code]net_thread_cpu_seconds[/code] (CPU time of the readahead thread). For http://, https:// and udp:// streams: [code]net_buffer_bytes[/code], [code]net_buffered_bytes[/code], [code]net_bytes_read[/code], [code]net_requests[/code] (HTTP requests made: the first, one per seek outside the ring, one per reconnect), [code]net_resets[/code] (seeks outside the buffered range), [code]net_waits[/code] and [code]net_wait_seconds[/code] (reads that had to wait for the network), [code]net_reconnects[/code], [code]net_errors[/code], [code]net_packets[/code] (UDP datagrams), [code]net_overruns[/code] (bytes of a live stream dropped unread: the ring was full, or the reader fell behind), [code]net_skips[/code] (times a live stream skipped ahead because it was read more than twice [member live_latency] late), [code]net_wakeups[/code] (turns of the reader thread: for UDP, one per batch of datagrams, about 100 a second at most), [code]net_average_mbps[/code] (since open) and [code]net_thread_cpu_seconds[/code].

method.name: get_subtitle_header
method.description: Returns the ASS header ([code][Script Info][/code], [code][V4+ Styles][/code], [code][Events][/code] format) of the selected text subtitle track, for libass. Empty for bitmap tracks, and until the demux thread has opened the track's decoder.

method.name: get_subtitle_lines
method.description: Returns every line of a text subtitle track (the file's own, or a file added with [method add_external_subtitle]), one Dictionary each: [code]start[/code] and [code]end[/code] (media seconds, sorted by start; where the file gives no end, the next line's start, or 5 s after the last line), [code]text[/code] (plain text, override tags removed, lines separated by [code]\n[/code]) and [code]ass[/code] (FFmpeg's ASS event line, as in [method read_subtitle_event]; FFmpeg makes one for SubRip and WebVTT too). For a list of all the lines, to search them or jump to one. Blocking: call it on a worker thread. An added file's lines are copied at once. A track of the file's own is read with a demux context of its own, so playback isn't touched, but the whole file is read, as the subtitle packets are spread through it: about as long as copying the file (100 MB/s on the desktop test machine: 8 s for 800 MB, 23 s for 2.1 GB, with about 7 % of a core, mostly in file reads). Over smb:// or http(s):// it shares the network with playback. [method close] stops a read in progress (empty result; [method get_last_error] says so). Empty, with [method get_last_error] set, for a bitmap track, a track that isn't there and a live stream; the source stays usable. Any thread.

method.name: get_subtitle_track
method.description: Returns the selected subtitle track, or -1.

method.name: get_subtitle_tracks
method.description: Returns one Dictionary per subtitle stream: [code]index[/code], [code]stream_index[/code], [code]codec[/code], [code]text[/code] (decoded to text: SubRip, ASS/SSA, MP4 timed text, WebVTT), [code]bitmap[/code] (PGS, VobSub, DVB, XSUB), [code]bitmap_decoded[/code] (a bitmap track whose events carry images; else they carry the raw packets), [code]language[/code], [code]language_code[/code] ([method normalize_language]), [code]title[/code], [code]default[/code], [code]forced[/code], [code]hearing_impaired[/code] (both also from the title), [code]external[/code], and for subtitle files ([method add_external_subtitle]) [code]path[/code]. The file's own tracks come first.

method.name: get_tags
method.description: Returns the file's metadata tags with lower-case keys, as the container gives them: for music files usually [code]title[/code], [code]artist[/code], [code]album[/code], [code]album_artist[/code], [code]track[/code] ("3" or "3/12"), [code]disc[/code], [code]date[/code], [code]genre[/code], [code]comment[/code]. The container's tags come first, then the first audio stream's (Ogg keeps its comments there) for keys not yet given. Technical tags ([code]encoder[/code], [code]handler_name[/code], brands) are left out. Empty before [method open].

method.name: get_tone_mapping
method.description: What a shader needs to show HDR video (PQ or HLG) on an SDR display whose peak is [param target_nits], from [method get_video_info]'s dictionary. 203 nits is the BT.2408 reference white; raise it for a brighter picture with more compressed highlights, lower it for the opposite. The returned Dictionary: [code]transfer[/code] ("pq", "hlg" or "sdr"), [code]gamut_matrix[/code] (a [Basis] from linear light in the video's primaries to linear BT.709: BT.2020 or P3 to BT.709, identity for BT.709; in a shader, a [code]mat3[/code] uniform set from it gives [code]gamut * rgb[/code]; clamp negative results), [code]primaries_bt709[/code], the PQ constants [code]pq_m1[/code], [code]pq_m2[/code], [code]pq_c1[/code], [code]pq_c2[/code], [code]pq_c3[/code] (SMPTE ST 2084), the HLG constants [code]hlg_a[/code], [code]hlg_b[/code], [code]hlg_c[/code] and [code]hlg_system_gamma[/code] (1.2, a 1000 nit display, [code]hlg_peak_nits[/code]), [code]source_peak_nits[/code] (MaxCLL, else the mastering display's peak, else 1000; never above the mastering display's peak), [code]source_black_nits[/code], [code]target_peak_nits[/code], and the BT.2390 EETF's [code]source_min_pq[/code], [code]source_max_pq[/code], [code]max_luminance[/code] and [code]knee_start[/code], with [code]tone_mapping[/code] ([code]false[/code] when the source fits the target or is SDR). Per pixel, after Y'CbCr to R'G'B' (BT.2020 matrix): (1) R'G'B' to light in nits: PQ EOTF, or for HLG the inverse OETF and the OOTF ([code]scene * 1000 * Y^(gamma - 1)[/code]). (2) [code]gamut_matrix[/code], clamp at 0. (3) If [code]tone_mapping[/code], on the brightest channel M: [code]E = (PQ(M) - source_min_pq) / (source_max_pq - source_min_pq)[/code]; above [code]knee_start[/code] replace E with the Hermite spline [code](2t³ - 3t² + 1) ks + (t³ - 2t² + t)(1 - ks) + (-2t³ + 3t²) max_luminance[/code], [code]t = (E - ks) / (1 - ks)[/code]; scale all three channels by [code]EOTF(E (source_max_pq - source_min_pq) + source_min_pq) / M[/code], which keeps the hue. (4) Divide by [code]target_peak_nits[/code]: linear light, 1.0 being display white (Godot's ALBEDO). [method tone_map_color] does the same on the CPU, and the player spike's [code]video.gdshader[/code] does it in GLSL.

method.name: get_trick_play_speed
method.description: Returns the speed of [method trick_play], or 0 during normal playback.

method.name: get_video_bitrate_history
method.description: Returns the video bit rate in kbit/s of each of the [param seconds] whole media seconds before [param at] (the playback position), oldest first, from the sizes of the packets read; -1 where it isn't known (not read since the last [method seek], or more than about 64 s from the read position). At most 64 values. For a bitrate graph; [method HWVideoTexture.get_overlay_stats] includes the last 60 s.

method.name: get_video_info
method.description: Returns the video stream: [code]codec[/code] ("h264", "hevc", "vp9", "av1" or FFmpeg's name), [code]is_h264[/code], [code]is_hevc[/code], [code]is_vp9[/code], [code]is_av1[/code], [code]width[/code], [code]height[/code] (the cropped picture size, before any pixel aspect; the exact visible rectangle comes from [method HWVideoTexture.get_visible_rect]), [code]sample_aspect_ratio[/code] (pixel aspect, 1 if square or unknown), [code]display_aspect[/code], [code]fps[/code], [code]bit_depth[/code], [code]profile[/code], [code]pixel_format[/code], the colour description [code]color_primaries[/code], [code]color_transfer[/code], [code]color_matrix[/code], [code]color_range[/code] (FFmpeg's names such as "bt709", "bt2020nc", "smpte2084", "tv"; empty if unspecified) and from it [code]matrix_bt2020[/code], [code]full_range[/code] and [code]hdr[/code] (PQ or HLG transfer: needs tone mapping, see [method get_tone_mapping]), the HDR metadata [code]hdr_transfer[/code] ("pq", "hlg" or ""), [code]max_cll[/code] and [code]max_fall[/code] (nits; 0 if not given), [code]mastering_display_primaries[/code] (a [PackedVector2Array] of CIE 1931 x, y for red, green, blue and the white point; empty if not given), [code]mastering_display_luminance[/code] (a [Vector2]: minimum and maximum nits; zero if not given), [code]hdr_metadata_source[/code] ("container", "sei" (most rips: read from the first keyframe at open, which costs a few milliseconds), "container+sei" or ""), [code]dolby_vision_profile[/code] (from the container's configuration record; -1 if none; the base layer plays as HDR10, the Dolby Vision layer is ignored), [code]hdr10plus[/code] (HDR10+ dynamic metadata in the first keyframe; ignored),[code]hw_decodable[/code] (the Frame can decode and show it in hardware: H.264 or HEVC, 4:2:0, 8-bit, or 10-bit when the decoder offers P010), [code]hw_unsupported_reason[/code] (why not, as a sentence for the user; empty if it can), [code]software_decodable[/code] (not in hardware, but [HWVideoTexture] decodes it in software: H.264, HEVC or VP9 up to about 1080p), [code]playable[/code] (one or the other), [code]unplayable_reason[/code] (why neither), [code]annexb_filter[/code], and from the SPS [code]coded_width[/code], [code]coded_height[/code], [code]display_width[/code], [code]display_height[/code], [code]chroma_format[/code], and [code]field_order[/code] (FFmpeg's names: "progressive", or for interlaced video "tt", "bb", "tb", "bt": the field coded first, then the field shown first, so "tt" and "bt" show the top field first; empty if the file doesn't say). Empty if there is no video. The container's stereo 3D and spherical metadata (Matroska StereoMode and Projection, MP4 st3d and sv3d), empty or zero when it says nothing (then guess from the file name): [code]stereo_mode[/code] ("2d", "sbs", "tb", "frame_sequence", "checkerboard", "sbs_quincunx", "lines", "columns", or "unspecified" when the file says only that it has two views, as Apple's MP4 boxes do), [code]stereo_inverted[/code] (the right eye's picture comes first), [code]stereo_mode_tag[/code] (Matroska's StereoMode as its stream tag, such as "left_right" or "bottom_top"; empty otherwise), [code]stereo_baseline_mm[/code], [code]stereo_fov[/code] (degrees), [code]projection[/code] ("equirectangular", "half_equirectangular", "cubemap", "fisheye", "rectilinear", "parametric_immersive", "other"), [code]projection_fov[/code] (degrees across and down, a [Vector2]: 360x180 for a full equirectangular sphere, 180x180 for VR180, 0 if unknown), [code]projection_yaw_pitch_roll[/code] (degrees, a [Vector3]) and [code]projection_bounds[/code] (the equirectangular crop: left, top, right, bottom as fractions of the full sphere, a [Vector4]).

method.name: read_audio_frames
method.description: Takes [param count] stereo frames of the decoded audio at [method get_output_rate], as the [AudioStreamPlayer] of [method get_audio_stream] would: silence where none is decoded yet, and [method get_audio_position] moves the same way. For audio that leaves the device without the audio server, for example sent to a PC. Use it instead of [method get_audio_stream], not beside it: both take from the same buffer. Call it from one thread at a time. With [method set_external_clock], the audio is resampled by up to 0.5 % so that [method get_audio_position] follows that clock. The rate changes by 5 % of the gap per second, so a gap of 0.1 s closes to 61 ms in 10 s (exponentially, by half in about 14 s); fix larger gaps with [method seek]. [code]external_clock_error_ms[/code] and [code]external_clock_ratio[/code] in [method get_stats] show the gap and the rate.

method.name: read_subtitle_event
method.description: Takes the next event of the selected subtitle track: [code]start[/code] and [code]end[/code] (media seconds; [code]end[/code] is -1 when unknown, as for most bitmap tracks, where the next event ends it), [code]text[/code] (plain text, lines separated by [code]\n[/code], ASS override tags removed), [code]ass[/code] (FFmpeg's ASS event line(s): ReadOrder, Layer, Style, Name, margins, Effect, Text), [code]bitmap[/code], [code]serial[/code], [code]track[/code] (the subtitle track the event is from: with dual subtitles, see [method select_secondary_subtitle_track]). Text tracks also give [code]styled[/code]: an Array with one Dictionary per ASS line of the event, as [method parse_ass_event] returns them (runs of styled text, alignment, position, margins, script resolution). Bitmap tracks (PGS, VobSub, DVB, XSUB) are decoded to pictures: [code]images[/code] (an Array of Dictionaries: [code]rect[/code], a [Rect2i] in the canvas's pixels; [code]image[/code], an RGBA8 [Image] of the rect's size with straight alpha; [code]forced[/code]), [code]forced[/code] (any of them is), [code]canvas_size[/code] (the [Vector2i] the rects are in, usually the video's size; scale it to the video's rectangle). An event without images clears the screen from its start: PGS sends one after each picture, and most bitmap events have no [code]end[/code]. A bitmap track without a decoder gives [code]data[/code] (the raw packet) instead. Returns an empty Dictionary when none is queued. Events come in file order, about the queue length ahead of the playback position; keep them until their time. At most 512 are queued (the oldest are dropped). Subtitle files ([method add_external_subtitle]) hand out all their events at once instead. For a negative subtitle delay, see [member subtitle_read_ahead].

method.name: select_secondary_subtitle_track
method.description: Dual subtitles: reads a second text track of the file's own (-1: none) alongside the track of [method select_subtitle_track], which can also be a subtitle file. Its events come through [method read_subtitle_event] too, in file order, each with [code]track[/code] saying which track it is from; [code]styled[/code] uses that track's own ASS header. Subtitle files and bitmap tracks can't be the second track: for a second file, show its lines from [method get_subtitle_lines]. Like [method select_subtitle_track], this doesn't seek.

method.name: select_subtitle_track
method.description: Selects a subtitle track (-1: none). This doesn't seek: events whose packets were read before (up to the queue length ahead of the playback position) aren't delivered. An event that started before a seek target isn't delivered after the seek either, unless its packet lies after the keyframe the seek lands on.

method.name: is_eof
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] once the file is read to the end (queued data may still be waiting).

method.name: is_live
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] for a live stream: [code]udp://[/code], or HTTP whose server gives no length. It plays as it arrives and can't seek. If it isn't read for longer than twice [member live_latency], the oldest data is skipped ([code]net_skips[/code] in [method get_stats]).

method.name: is_open
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] between a successful [method open] and [method close].

method.name: is_seekable
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] when [method seek] works: an open file, or an HTTP stream whose server takes Range requests. [code]false[/code] for live streams and for servers that only send the whole file.

method.name: language_name
method.description: Returns the English name of a language code or name, normalized first: [code]"ger"[/code] gives [code]"German"[/code], [code]"pt-BR"[/code] gives [code]"Portuguese (BR)"[/code]. Unknown codes come back as given.

method.name: normalize_language
method.description: Returns the ISO 639-1 code for a language as containers and file names give it: ISO 639-2/B and /T codes ([code]"ger"[/code], [code]"deu"[/code]), ISO 639-1 codes, and English names ([code]"German"[/code]) all give [code]"de"[/code]. Lower case, with a region kept after a hyphen ([code]"pt_BR"[/code] gives [code]"pt-br"[/code]). [code]"und"[/code] and other "no language" codes give an empty string; unknown codes come back lower case.

method.name: open
method.description: Opens a file, reads its stream information, selects the default audio track and starts reading. Blocks while it reads the start of the file. [param path] is a local path, a [code]res://[/code] or [code]user://[/code] path, or [code]smb://host/share/path/file[/code] (not URL-encoded: names are written as they are). For an smb:// file, the host is connected and logged into with the credentials of [method set_smb_credentials] (else as guest), which can take up to about 8 s per step when the host doesn't answer: open from a worker thread if the caller must not stall. Errors are sentences for the user in [method get_last_error], for example "Access denied: HOST refused the user name or password." or "Not found: share/path on HOST.". [param path] can also be a URL. [code]http://host[:port]/path[/code] and [code]https://...[/code] use HTTP/1.1 with Range requests, so the file seeks like a local one; up to 5 redirects are followed and chunked replies are read. A server without Range support plays from the start without seeking. A lost connection is opened again where it stopped (5 tries). [code]udp://[group]:port[/code] is MPEG-TS in UDP datagrams: [code]udp://@:1234[/code] listens on every interface, and a multicast group is joined on every interface. A thread of their own reads streams into a ring of [member network_buffer_size] bytes. For a live stream, open reads at most about [member live_latency] of it to find the streams. Joining mid-stream, it returns once the next keyframe has come: live TV sends one every 0.5 to 2 s. Playback then starts when [member live_latency] of audio is buffered. HTTPS checks the server's certificate against the system's CA store (or [code]network/tls/certificate_bundle_override[/code]) unless [member network_tls_verify] is off. FFmpeg's own network code isn't used.

method.name: parse_ass_event
method.description: Parses one ASS event line as FFmpeg gives it ([code]ReadOrder,Layer,Style,Name,MarginL,MarginR,MarginV,Effect,Text[/code]) against an ASS or SSA script header ([method get_subtitle_header]; empty: ASS's defaults) into what an app can draw without libass. The result is the same as each entry of [method read_subtitle_event]'s [code]styled[/code], which already does this for text tracks: [code]runs[/code]: an Array of Dictionaries, one per stretch of text with the same style: [code]text[/code] (line breaks as [code]\n[/code], [code]\h[/code] as a no-break space), [code]font[/code], [code]size[/code] (in script pixels), [code]color[/code], [code]outline_color[/code], [code]outline_width[/code], [code]bold[/code], [code]italic[/code], [code]underline[/code], [code]strikeout[/code]. [code]text[/code] (all runs as plain text), [code]alignment[/code] (numpad layout: 1-3 bottom, 4-6 middle, 7-9 top; left, centre, right), [code]position[/code] (from [code]\pos[/code], in script pixels; (-1, -1) if none: place by alignment and margins), [code]margin_l[/code], [code]margin_r[/code], [code]margin_v[/code], [code]play_res[/code] (the script resolution that sizes, positions and margins are in, a [Vector2i]; 384x288 when the script doesn't say, as for SubRip), [code]style[/code], [code]layer[/code], [code]back_color[/code] (the style's shadow or box colour). Override tags read: [code]\b[/code], [code]\i[/code], [code]\u[/code], [code]\s[/code], [code]\fn[/code], [code]\fs[/code], [code]\c[/code]/[code]\1c[/code], [code]\3c[/code], [code]\1a[/code]/[code]\alpha[/code], [code]\bord[/code], [code]\r[/code], [code]\an[/code], [code]\a[/code], [code]\pos[/code]; a tag without a value goes back to the style's value. Others (karaoke, [code]\t[/code], [code]\move[/code], [code]\clip[/code], drawings, rotation, blur, fades) are dropped. SubRip's [code]<b>[/code], [code]<i>[/code], [code]<u>[/code] and [code]<font color>[/code] reach here as override tags.

method.name: pick_audio_track
method.description: Language memory: returns the audio track that fits [param languages] (codes or names, the most preferred first) best, or -1 if none is in any of them. Among tracks of the same language: not a commentary, not audio description, the default flag, then more channels. A preference without a region matches every region; one with a region matches only that region.

method.name: pick_subtitle_track
method.description: Language memory: returns the subtitle track (the file's own and the added files) that fits [param languages] best, or -1. Among tracks of the same language: text before bitmap (only text is drawn so far), full before forced, without before with hearing-impaired notes, the default flag, the file's own before a file. With [param forced_only], only forced tracks count (the foreign parts of a film whose audio is in the viewer's language).

method.name: read_video_packet
method.description: For scripts and tests: takes the next video access unit from the queue and returns [code]data[/code] (a copy), [code]pts[/code], [code]dts[/code], [code]keyframe[/code], [code]serial[/code], [code]sps_width[/code], [code]sps_height[/code] (coded size of an SPS in it, or 0), [code]nal_type[/code] and [code]random_access[/code] (for keyframes and the first access unit after a seek: the first picture NAL unit type, and "idr", "cra", "bla" or "i" for an H.264 non-IDR I picture; -1 and "" otherwise). Returns an empty Dictionary if none is queued yet. Don't use it while a [V4L2Decoder] reads the same source.

method.name: seek
method.description: Drops everything queued and reads again from the keyframe at or before [param seconds]. Containers without a keyframe index (MPEG-TS) are seeked by timestamp: when the first keyframe found is after the target, the file is seeked again 2, 4, 8... s earlier (up to 6 times; [code]seek_retries[/code] in [method get_stats]), with the audio read meanwhile held back. Decoded audio before the target is dropped (and a short gap filled with silence), so the audio clock restarts exactly at the target. A [HWVideoTexture] playing this source notices the new serial, drops its stale frames and shows the frame at the target. Returns the new serial. Any thread.

method.name: select_audio_track
method.description: Selects an audio track (-1: none). While open, this seeks to the current position, because the queues already hold the old track's audio.

method.name: set_external_clock
method.description: Sets an external master clock for [method read_audio_frames]: at [method Time.get_ticks_usec] [param ticks_usec] the media time was [param seconds], and it runs on in real time from there. Set it again whenever the master clock is read (for example with each timestamp from the network). It is compared with [method get_audio_position], which is the frame last taken: if that frame is heard later (a buffer on the PC), add that latency to [param seconds]. [param seconds] below 0: no external clock. Any thread.

method.name: set_smb_credentials
method.description: Sets the credentials for smb:// files on [param host] (as it appears in the URL; not case-sensitive), shared with [MediaBrowser] ([method MediaBrowser.set_smb_credentials] is the same). [param domain] is the host's computer name or workgroup for a local account, or empty. An empty user and password remove the entry. Kept in memory only; never logged, never part of a path. NTLMSSP authentication; signing is used when the server requires it (AES-CMAC, with the CPU's AES instructions when it has them).

method.name: trick_play
method.description: Fast forward. [param speed] 2 to 64: only keyframes are read and queued, from the keyframe at or before [param from], at most one per 0.25 s of wall time ([param speed] x 0.25 s apart in media time). With an index (Matroska, MP4, AVI) the reader jumps from keyframe to keyframe and reads nothing in between ([code]trick_steps[/code] in [method get_stats]). Without one (MPEG-TS) it reads on and drops the rest. There is no audio: the audio stream plays silence and [code]audio_finished[/code] is [code]true[/code]. A [HWVideoTexture] playing this source runs its clock at [param speed] meanwhile and ignores the master clock it is given. [param speed] under 2: normal playback again, with audio, from [param from] (pass [method HWVideoTexture.get_position]). Either way it is a [method seek]: returns the new serial. A [method seek] during trick play stays in trick play. Live streams can't seek, so they have no trick play.

method.name: tone_map_color
method.description: [method get_tone_mapping]'s steps on the CPU for one R'G'B' value as decoded (non-linear, 0 to 1): returns linear BT.709 RGB, 1.0 being the target peak. For tests, and to check a shader against; far too slow for pictures.

members.member: FFmpeg options for the audio decoder (AVOptions, as strings), applied when a track's decoder opens. For example [code]{"core_only": "1"}[/code] makes the DTS decoder ignore the DTS-HD extensions (XLL lossless, XBR, X96) and decode the core only, as a cheaper fallback. Options a decoder doesn't know are ignored. Set before [method open]. FFmpeg's AC-3 / E-AC-3 decoder forgets its options when it is flushed: MediaSource sets them again after every seek. A [code]"drc_scale"[/code] here overrides [member night_mode]'s.
Decoded audio to keep ahead of the playback position. Set before [method open].

Dialogue boost in dB (0 to 12): the centre channel, where films put the dialogue, is that much louder in the downmix to stereo. Only for audio with a centre channel next to front left and right (5.1, 7.1, 3.0, ...; see [code]dialogue_boost_applies[/code] in [method get_stats]); stereo and mono stay as they are. A limiter keeps the peaks below -1 dBFS while it is above 0. Can be changed at any time; it is heard after the audio queue ([member audio_queue_seconds]), at once after a seek.

If [code]true[/code], the audio is also kept as 7.1 float channels (FL FR FC LFE BL BR SL SR), each playable through [method get_audio_channel_stream]. The resampler then makes 7.1 and the stereo mix is the downmix of those channels (the same mix as without). It costs a second ring of 8 channels (about 5.6 MB at 44.1 kHz) and, on x86, about 0.1 % of a core. Set before [method open].
If [code]true[/code], the downmix to stereo is scaled so no sum can exceed full scale (about 7.7 dB quieter for 5.1). Set before [method open].

If [code]true[/code], [method open] starts a thread that looks for black bars, with the result in [method get_letterbox]. The hardware decoder's frames can't be read by the CPU, so the thread decodes keyframes itself with FFmpeg's software decoder (H.264, HEVC, VP9; one thread, no loop filter, at a low priority): one every 4 s of media time as the file is read, then every 15 s after the first 16. In each, luma rows and then columns are scanned in from the edges until one has more than 2 % of its samples above black. Frames that are black, or whose picture is too dark on average, don't count (a dark scene's edges look like bars). Each edge of the result is the outermost of the frames', leaving out the single outermost when there are 4 frames or more (a logo or a flash over the bars). Bars under 1 % of the size are ignored, and so are bars on one axis that differ by more than 1.5 % from each other (bars are centred). On x86 a 1080p H.264 keyframe takes about 5 to 40 ms, a 2160p HEVC one 60 to 100 ms; the result comes after about 20 to 60 s of media (minutes for a film that opens in the dark). Set before [method open].

Seconds (0.1 to 2.5) of a live stream ([method is_live]) to buffer before playing. The audio stream plays silence and its clock stands until this much decoded audio is buffered, after [method open] and again after an underrun, so the buffer absorbs that much network jitter. [method open] analyses up to this much (at least 0.3 s) to find the streams, and the thread keeps at least this much audio (plus 0.25 s) decoded ahead, more than [member audio_queue_seconds] if need be. Once the reader is more than twice this behind the newest data, the stream skips ahead. Smaller starts sooner and stays closer to live; larger rides out more jitter. A live stream without audio has no pre-roll. Set before [method open].

Size in bytes of the readahead ring of smb://, http://, https:// and udp:// streams (4 MiB to 256 MiB; applies at the next [method open]). For smb:// files: reads of up to 1 MiB, up to 4 in flight; 1/8 of the ring is kept behind the read position for short backward seeks, the rest is read ahead. After a seek outside the ring the readahead starts at 256 KiB and doubles as the file is read on. A lost connection is reopened (5 tries, 0.5 s to 8 s apart) and the reading resumes where it stopped; after that the source goes to [constant STATE_ERROR] with the reason in [method get_last_error].

If [code]true[/code], an https:// server must show a certificate that the system's CA store (or [code]network/tls/certificate_bundle_override[/code]) trusts, for the host name in the URL. If not, [method open] fails with "The TLS handshake with HOST failed (a certificate that isn't trusted?).". Set it to [code]false[/code] for a server on the local network with a self-signed certificate: the connection is still encrypted, but anyone in the path could pose as the server. Set before [method open].
Read requests (of up to 1 MiB) in flight at once for smb:// files, 1 to 16; applies at the next [method open]. More keeps a link with more latency busy.

Night mode: loud passages are turned down and quiet ones up, for listening at low volume. AC-3 and E-AC-3 tracks get the decoder's own dynamic range compression from the stream's metadata (scaled by [member night_mode_strength]; without night mode it is off, the full range). Most rips carry none, so every track also goes through a compressor after the downmix: a typical level learnt over about 5 s, a leveller towards -24 dBFS (up to +12 dB, down to -6 dB), a 5:1 compressor above the typical level, a gentle lift for passages more than 6 dB below it, and a limiter at -1 dBFS. On five films it halved the spread between the 10th and 95th percentile of 400 ms levels (from 15-34 dB to 8-15 dB). The cost is a few multiply-adds per sample, on the demux thread. Can be changed at any time; it is heard after the audio queue ([member audio_queue_seconds]), at once after a seek. [method get_stats] shows [code]night_mode_decoder_drc[/code], [code]audio_gain_db[/code], [code]audio_limiter_db[/code] and [code]audio_typical_level_db[/code].
How strong [member night_mode] is, 0 to 1: the decoder's DRC scale, the compressor's ratio (1 + 4 x strength) and the leveller's largest boost (12 dB x strength).

0.5 to 2. The audio plays faster or slower with its pitch kept (a WSOLA time stretch in the mixer: about 0.3 % of an x86 core at any speed other than 1, nothing at 1), and as the audio clock is the master clock, the video follows; the decoder then has to decode that much faster. Takes effect at the next mix, any time. The output latency corrections of the clock ([method AudioServer.get_time_since_last_mix], [method AudioServer.get_output_latency]) are in real seconds: multiply them by the speed. Without an audio track, set [member HWVideoTexture.playback_speed] instead.

Seconds (0 to 30). The events of a file's own subtitle tracks come with its packets, about [member video_queue_seconds] ahead of the playback. A negative subtitle delay (showing lines earlier) needs them earlier than that: set this to the largest such delay, and while a subtitle track of the file is selected the video is read that far ahead (plus 0.5 s), within the queue's limits of 512 packets and 96 MiB (about 20 s at 24 fps). Costs memory, not CPU. The delay itself is applied by whoever shows the lines. Subtitle files don't need it.
Video access units to keep queued, in seconds of frames. Set before [method open].

constants.constant: The whole file was read; what is queued can still be consumed. A [method seek] reads again.
